hints: Focus on what pi bonding means for C5H10, it points to alkenes with C=C and rules out cycloalkanes which have only sigma bonds.
Start by listing the structural alkene skeletons: straight-chain pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene, plus branched methylbutenes.
Now check each C=C for E/Z stereoisomerism by seeing if each carbon of the double bond has two different groups, then add any extra stereoisomer to your total.
walkthrough:
**Decide what counts as pi bonding**

Great start, let's narrow it down. Formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$ fits the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$, so it could be an alkene or a cycloalkane.

Only alkenes contain a $\text{C=C}$ double bond with pi bonding, cycloalkanes have only single sigma bonds, so we count alkene isomers only.

**Draw the straight-chain structural isomers**

Let's build the unbranched chain first. We can place the double bond at position 1 or 2:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (pent-1-ene)}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (pent-2-ene)}$$

**Draw the branched structural isomers**

Now add a methyl branch to a 4-carbon chain. There are three distinct positions for the double bond:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (2-methylbut-1-ene)}$$
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3 \text{ (3-methylbut-1-ene)}$$
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3 \text{ (2-methylbut-2-ene)}$$
So far that is 2 straight-chain + 3 branched = 5 structural isomers.

**Add stereoisomerism**

This is the key Cambridge trap. Check for E/Z (cis-trans) isomerism where each C of C=C has two different groups.

Only pent-2-ene qualifies, giving cis (Z) and trans (E) forms. The terminal alkenes and the highly substituted 2-methylbut-2-ene do not show it.

Total = 5 structural + 1 extra stereoisomer = 6 isomers with pi bonding.

options.A: 3 is far too low. It counts only some structural isomers and misses both branched alkenes and stereoisomerism. You must systematically list all C=C positions and branch positions.
options.B: 4 misses isomers. A common error is to count only 4 structural alkenes or to forget that pent-2-ene exists as two stereoisomers, E and Z.
options.C: 5 counts the 5 structural alkene skeletons correctly but forgets stereoisomerism. Pent-2-ene has cis and trans forms, so one must be added to reach the full total.
options.D: 6 is correct. There are 5 structural alkenes: pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, plus pent-2-ene splits into E and Z, giving 6 pi-bonded isomers in total.
